request.questionText: O's Cafe offers a pizza lunch during which each customer selects exactly one slice of pizza, choosing either cheese or pepperoni. It is known that customers are thrice as likely* to choose cheese relative to pepperoni. Assuming that the pizza selection of one resident does not affect those of others, which of the following statements is TRUE? On a regular day with 80 customers, 20 of them are expected to choose pepperoni pizza. On a busy day with 120 customers, the probability that no more than 30 of them will choose pepperoni pizza is 0.25. On a slow day with 40 customers, the probability that all 40 of them will choose cheese pizza is 1. * In other words, three out of every four slices selected are cheese; there is a 25% probability that a customer selects pepperoni.
